tasks.text: 早安！我姓王，名字叫小文。小姐，您貴姓？——我姓張，名字叫安妮。王小姐，您好！——張小姐，您好！
tasks.question: 王小姐叫什麼名字？
tasks.why: The first person's surname is 王 and given name 小文; the second person calls her 王小姐 → 王小文 (this full name is never written in one piece). A: the second person's name. C and D: the two people's surnames and given names are mixed up.

grammar.explain: 是 links the subject to its identity (= 'to be'). It is not used with adjectives: not *我是好, but 我很好 (coming in A07).

catatan.rujukan: 《看圖學中文語法・基礎篇》 Unit 3
note: Three verbs for introducing someone: 姓 + surname (她姓王), 叫 + name (她叫王秋華 / 她叫秋華), 是 + identity (她是王秋華、她是醫生).
After 姓 comes only the surname: ✗ 她姓王秋華. A job takes 是, not 叫: ✗ 她叫醫生 → ✓ 她是醫生.
Negative: 不 before the verb — 不姓李、不叫秋月、不是老師. Short answers: 是 / 不(是).

grammar.explain: A question word stays in the position of the answer — it does not move to the front. To answer, replace 什麼 with the information: 你叫什麼名字？→ 我叫王大文。

check.q: The answer to 你叫什麼名字？

catatan.rujukan: 《看圖學中文語法・基礎篇》 Unit 10
note: 什麼 can be followed directly by a noun to ask WHAT KIND: 這是什麼? → 這是蛋糕. 這是什麼蛋糕? → 這是水果蛋糕.
To answer, put the answer where 什麼 was; the word order stays the same: 你要買什麼? → 我要買手套.

supplement.note: This 義項 = a polite form of address. 貴 'expensive' is learned in the shopping scene.

grammar.explain: Add 嗎 to the end of a statement; the word order does NOT change. Answer by repeating the verb: 你說英文嗎？→ 說。

check.q: Turn it into a question: 他是美國人。

catatan.rujukan: 《看圖學中文語法・基礎篇》 Unit 4–5
note: Yes/no questions can also use the A-not-A pattern: 你是不是臺灣人？ = 你是臺灣人嗎？ Both are answered by repeating the verb: 是 / 不是.
Do not use 嗎 together with a question word (哪、誰、什麼、幾): ✗ 你是哪國人嗎？ ✓ 你是哪國人？

grammar.point: 哪 — which (這/那 come in A03)
grammar.explain: 哪 = 'which', placed where the answer goes: 你是哪國人？→ 我是印尼人。 Sentences with question words like 哪/什麼 do NOT use 嗎.

examples.zh: 他是哪國人？他是美國人。
examples.id: Where is he from? He's American.

catatan.rujukan: 《看圖學中文語法・基礎篇》 Unit 4
note: 哪 asks 'which one' among several choices; to ask about the person (who) use 誰: 誰是日本人？
You can also ask where someone is from with 從哪裡來: 你從哪裡來？ — 我從印尼來。
哪 can be followed directly by a number + measure word: 哪(一)位老師？ 哪兩個人？

core.note: One-character form, used INSIDE words: 哪國人、美國、外國. It does not stand alone as "country".

supplement.note: The stand-alone word for "country": 這個國家很大。 我們國家.

supplement.meaning: can (ability; 會說中文 = can speak Mandarin)
particle; in 是的 = yes, that's right (a full, polite "yes")
supplement.note: In A02, 的 only appears in 是的. The main use of 的 as a possessive marker (我的爸爸 = my father) is learned in the next unit.

grammar.point: 數 + 量 — number + measure word
grammar.explain: Between a number and a noun there must be a measure word (量詞). 個 is the most common. For 'two' before a 量詞 use 兩: 兩個人, not 二個人.

examples.id: There are five people in my family.

catatan.rujukan: 《看圖學中文語法・基礎篇》 Unit 1–2, 5
note: The measure word depends on the kind of thing: 個 (general: people, things), 位 (people, polite: 一位老師), 本 (books), 張 (flat things: 紙、桌子), 件 (tops), 條 (long things: 褲子、魚), 雙 (pairs: 鞋子), 隻 (animals), 杯/瓶/碗 (containers).
這/那/哪 + number + measure word + noun: 這兩個人、那三本書. Without a number it means one: 這個人. 這些/那些 = plural, without a number: 那些書.
Possession is negated with 沒有, never 不有: 我沒有弟弟。 Question form: 你有沒有哥哥？

grammar.point: 稱數法 — how to say numbers
grammar.explain: Mandarin numbers are built like arithmetic: 十一 (10+1), 二十 (2×10), 二十五 (2×10+5). When counting or saying a number use 二; before a 量詞 use 兩.

catatan.rujukan: 《看圖學中文語法・基礎篇》 Unit 7–8
note: The number 2 before a measure word is 兩, not 二: 兩個人、兩本書 (but 十二、二十 keep 二).
幾 is used when the expected number is small (about ≤ 10) and must take a measure word: 你家有幾個人？ For large or unknown numbers use 多少: 你有多少朋友？
A zero in the middle is read 零: 105 = 一百零五. A final round digit can be dropped: 150 = 一百五(十).

grammar.point: 時間表達 — saying dates & times
grammar.pattern: 年 → 月 → 號/日 (big to small)

grammar.explain: Repeat the verb/adjective with 不 in the middle: 高不高, 是不是, 像不像. It means the same as …嗎？, so DON'T add 嗎 as well (你高不高嗎 ✗). Adjectives in statements take 很, not 是.

note: Two ways to ask the same yes/no question: 他是不是老師? = 他是老師嗎? With 有 the form is 有沒有: 你家有沒有中文書? (✗ 有不有).
Answer with the verb itself, not "yes/no": 是 / 不是; 有 / 沒有; 熱 / 不熱.
Two-syllable words may be shortened: 漂亮不漂亮 → 漂不漂亮; 喜歡不喜歡 → 喜不喜歡.

catatan.point: Telling the time: 點、分、半、一刻、差
catatan.rujukan: 《看圖學中文語法・基礎篇》 Unit 15–16
note: X點 = X o'clock; X點Y分 = Y minutes past X: 九點二十分 = 9:20. 2 o'clock = 兩點 (not 二點).
半 = half (30 minutes): 六點半 = 6:30.
一刻 = a quarter (15 minutes): 七點一刻 = 7:15; 三刻 = 45 minutes: 七點三刻 = 7:45. (extra vocabulary)
差 = … to: 差五分八點 = five to eight = 7:55. Also 八點差五分. (extra vocabulary)
Minutes under 10 may take 零: 八點零五分 = 8:05.
Asking the time: 現在幾點？ (what time is it?) / 你幾點起床？ (what time do you get up?)

supplement.note: Minute as a POINT on the clock. Compare 分鐘 = how long.
Minute as a DURATION: 我等了十分鐘。 Compare 分 = minute on the clock (三點十分).
Duration in hours: 兩個小時 = for two hours. The most common word. Compare 點 = o'clock (兩點 = 2 o'clock).
Means the SAME as 小時 (兩個鐘頭 = two hours), more colloquial. Just recognise it; 小時 is enough when speaking.
"The time when" — points to a moment: 什麼時候？ (when?) 吃飯的時候 (when eating).
"Time" as an amount or chance: 我沒有時間。 (I have no time). To ask "when", use 什麼時候.

grammar.point: 「的」省略 — when 的 is used and when it is dropped
grammar.pattern: 我(的)媽媽 ／ 我的衣服 ／ 白的(衣服)
grammar.explain: There are two kinds of 省略 to tell apart: (1) 的 itself is dropped — 我媽媽 = 'my mom'; (2) the noun is dropped and 的 stays — 白的 = 'the white one'. For when 的 may be dropped and when it must stay, see the notes below.

examples.id: These are my mom's clothes. (first 的 dropped, second 的 required)
Do you like the red one or the white one?
My old shoes are the black ones.

catatan.point: When is 的 used, when is it dropped (省略)?
catatan.rujukan: 《看圖學中文語法・基礎篇》 Unit 6
note: 的 MAY be dropped when the owner is a pronoun (我、你、他、我們…) and what is "owned" is a close person or your own place: 我(的)家、我(的)爸爸、我(的)媽媽、我(的)哥哥、我(的)朋友. The more common forms: 我媽媽、我家.
我的媽媽 is not wrong, but it sounds stiffer or stresses 'MY mom, not someone else's'.
的 MUST stay for things, animals and other matters: 我的名字、我的東西、我的衣服、我的車子 (✗ 我名字、✗ 我衣服).
的 also MUST stay when the owner is a name or a noun: 美美的鞋子、媽媽的衣服、王秋華的妹妹.
Combined: 我爸爸的爸爸是我爺爺。/ 我媽媽的衣服 — the first 的 is dropped (family), the second is required.

catatan.point: The second kind of 省略: the NOUN is dropped, 的 stays
catatan.rujukan: 《看圖學中文語法・基礎篇》 Unit 6, 23–24
note: When the noun is already clear, owner + 的 is enough: 這杯咖啡是我的 (= this coffee is mine), 那個眼鏡是爺爺的.
Adjective + 的 = 'the … one': 大的貴，小的便宜; 白的 = 'the white one', 新的 = 'the new one'.
Don't drop both 的 and the noun: ✗ 我要白 → ✓ 我要白的 / 我要白的衣服.
有點 + adjective = a bit (usually something undesirable): 這件有點小。 The full pattern is in B20.
A 比 B + adjective = A is more … than B: 黑的比白的便宜。 Do not add 很: ✗ 黑的比白的很便宜。 The full pattern is in B19.
好看 = good-looking: 白的很好看。 Like 好吃 (A16), it is learned as one word; the 好 + V pattern is in B26.

note: A-not-A questions about the weather: 今天熱不熱？ — 不熱，可是有一點冷。
